At the same time, O'Brien raised concerns that the most talented up-and-coming British filmmakers are "often siphoned off, sometimes too soon and over-optimistically, into the studio system." "So now, with less funding, the independent sector has ended up becoming the research and development wing of the film industry in this country." On this, she pointed to the growing microdrama space as being full of "fresh voices trying to find a way to burst out."

O'Brien said too many indie movies are getting made without ambitions of making serious money, as the I, Daniel Blake and The Wind That Shakes the Barley EP called on funders to "say no more clearly."

"Too many projects that frankly aren’t good enough get made," she added. "A direct no is far more helpful than a maybe and it’s useful to have cogent reasoning as to why it’s not going to make the grade."

She said the "brutal truth" in the "diminishing" indie movie market is that "a film must have genuine theatrical potential for distributors to be interested." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

O'Brien's blueprint involves serious consideration of "quotas purely for domestic [British] films on streaming and pay TV services," which is "at the heart of the market failure for the sector."

She also called for financing these smaller projects to become less complex so that she doesn't end up "being on a Zoom with 20 lawyers bickering over the recoupment schedule."

"We need to find ways in which to enable the next generations to tell their stories," she said, passionately. "With some structural changes and simplifications, some slimming down and some radical thinking, we can boost and recharge the sector. With the right wind in its sails a small film can punch way above its weight and benefit the whole industry."

O'Brien harked back to a "chamber piece that was simple and manageable," her and Loach's Palme d'Or winning I, Daniel Blake .

"With enlightened funders who left us to get on with the job, creative, engaged distribution and sales partners and an audience who saw themselves reflected on the screen in this little story, we achieved a lot," she added. "That’s what we’re asking for."

Among the titles in […]
articles.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Utopai Studios has opened an office in Beverly Hills to serve as the new home for its growing Hollywood production operation.

The AI company, which has a presence in several global territories, has been increasingly active in building a slate of animated and live-action features as well as episodic series. Among the titles in the works are The Most Serious Fart , an animated feature based on the children’s book by Mike Bender, and Half Moon , a live-action feature written and directed by Hyo-joo Yang.

The company is also teaming with Ex Machina on Cortés , a feature about Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés starring Antonio Banderas. articles.title: Marvel Fans Aren’t Holding Back After We Got Our First Look At One Doomsday Hero
articles.summary: One Marvel hero isn't getting love from fans.
articles.content:
There are few movie franchises as popular as the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which is constantly expanding thanks to new projects arriving in theaters and streaming with a Disney+ subscription . While there's always excitement about upcoming Marvel movies , the Avengers: Doomsday is on another level entirely. The public recently got another look at the Doomsday cast via new posters, and fans aren't holding back their thoughts about one hero's appearance.

Alan Cumming might be clueless about Doomsday , but he's finally entered the chat with the above poster. This is the clearest look we've gotten of the X-Man's design, apart from a brief glance in the Avengers: Doomsday trailer . It's quite different from his look in the second X-Men movie .

Ouch. There are also plenty of memes in the responses as well, including the of-used clip of Steve Buscemi saying "How do you do, fellow kids?" from 30 Rock . Some fans aren't responding to Alan Cumming's new look as Nightcrawler, including his mane of white hair. And yes, there are plenty of folks comparing his appearance to late actor Gene Wilder .

That's a huge difference. Of course, the hours that it took for X-2 really paid off, as Alan Cumming (and Rebecca Romijn) looked incredible in that sequel. We'll just have to wait and see if fans change their mind when they get to see Nightcrawler in all his glory.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The holiday season is upon us and while we’re embarking on the most wonderful time of the year, it’s also the busiest. After all, as November closes out and once we get past Thanksgiving, we’ll be just a few short weeks away from Christmas and all of the festivities keeping things merry and bright. But even in the busiest of seasons, there is always time for movies and that’s where Pluto TV comes in. Earlier this year, the free streamer announced their Double Feature Fridays weekly movie series and now, ComicBook can exclusively reveal what Pluto TV has in store for December’s lineup and it’s a perfect mix of merry, bright, and action-packed — and there’s even a streaming debut.

Each Friday in the month of December, movie lovers can head to Pluto TV for a truly great double feature that offers some truly inspired, holiday ready pairings. The special holiday season lineup of Double Feature Fridays kicks off every Friday at 8p.m. ET on Pluto TV Spotlight and not only do you get two great movies back-to-back, but as the experiences is in partnership with Entertainment Tonight , each week correspondent Emily Curl sets the stage with an original segment that draws on Entertainment Tonight 's more than four decades of Hollywood access and archival interviews. Viewers get behind-the-scenes of the movies and the stars before settling in for the real main event, the movies themselves. Now, about that December Double Feature Fridays Lineup? Check that out for yourself below and start making your list and checking it twice — you know, for two movies.

December’s Double Feature Fridays kicks off with two very different kinds of holiday trouble: a desperate heist and a not-so-merry Christmas con. In Stranglehold , in the heart of Arkansas, a desperate stripper and her veteran husband gamble everything on a high-stakes heist. But when a gang of redneck gangsters and rival crews collide, a simple robbery turns into a neon-lit hell. Stranglehold stars Ashley Benson, Jake Lacy, Justin Long, and Ron Perlman.

Then there’s Bad Santa . Arguably the most outrageous Christmas tale ever told , a thieving Santa who doesn’t’ care if you’ve been naughty or nice. Hot on his trail are a security guard, a sexy bartender, and the one kid who’s convinced he’s the real deal. Bad Santa stars Billy Bob Thornton, Tony Cox, Lauren Graham, Bernie Mac, and Brett Kelly.

Celebrate the season with stories of love, family, and new beginnings with this pairing. In The Christmas Heartbeat , after surviving sudden cardiac arrest, a NY food critic is forced back home to a never-ending Christmas and a love she thought was gone. The film, in its streaming debut, stars Brittany Curran, Beverly D’Angelo and Joey Lawrence.

It’s paired with New Year’s Eve . Set in New York on New Year’s Eve, this romantic comedy celebrates love, hope, forgiveness, second chances, and fresh starts through the intertwining stories of couples and singles, told amid the pulse and promise of the most dazzling night of the year. The film stars Halle Berry, Jessica Biel, Jon Bon Jovi, Abigail Breslin, Robert De Niro, Zac Efron, Katherine Heigl, Ashton Kutcher, Sarah Jessica Parker, Michelle Pfeiffer, Hilary Swank, and Sofia Vergara.

With just one week to go before Christmas, enjoy two holiday comedies delivering Christmas magic, family mayhem, and a little bit of ghostly intervention. In A Sudden Case of Christmas , an American couple bring their 10-year-old daughter to her grandfather’s hotel in Italy to tell her that they are separating. Hoping to bring them back together, she asks to celebrate one last Christmas together, even though it’s August. The film stars Danny DeVito, Andie MacDowell, Wilmer Valderrama, Lucy DeVito, and Antonella Rose.

In Scrooged , Frank Cross is a mean TV executive with the perfect qualities of a modern-day Scrooge. Before the night is over, he’ll be visited by three ghosts from the past, present, and future. This modern take on Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol stars Bill Murray, Karen Allen, John Forsythe, John Glover, Bobcat Goldthwait, and Carole Kane.

Who says you have to watch traditional Christmas movies on Christmas? Trade the holiday cheer for high-stakes action as two unlikely duos find themselves in mayhem. In London Calling , after botching a hit, Tommy Ward flees to L.A. and strikes a deal: mentor his boss’s awkward son in exchange for a way home. But a routine job turns int a night of gunfights, killers, and chaos as the odd duo battles to survive and earn redemption. The film stars Josh Duhamel, Jeremy Ray Taylor, Rick Hoffman, and Aidan Gillen.

That film is paired with The Hitman’s Bodyguard , an outrageous action-comedy featuring an elite bodyguard and renowned hitman forced to work together. To succeed, they don’t just have to avoid getting killed…they have to avoid killing each other. The film stars Ryan Reynolds, Samuel L. Jackson, Gary Oldman, and Salma Hayek.

Double Feature Fridays pairings premiere every Friday at 8 p.m. ET on Pluto TV Spotlight before joining the Double Feature Fridays collection on demand, Which holiday pairing are you most excited for? Let us know in the comments!

EXCLUSIVE : The entire Gilmore Girls collection is back together in one (streaming) place. Exactly a decade after Gilmore Girls: A Year In the Life launched on Netflix on Christmas Day 2016, the four-part revival of the beloved mother-daughter dramedy will premiere at its new home, Hulu (and Disney+ for bundle subscribers).

This will make for a seamless transition as Gilmore Girls: A Day In the Life 's last day on Netflix is Dec. 24; it will pop up on Hulu the next day, Dec. 25.

The move marks the official end of Gilmore Girls ' franchise presence on Netflix, which spanned 12 years. Stemming from Amy Sherman-Palladino's longtime desire to end the story on her own terms after abruptly exiting the series ahead of Season 7 following failed contract negotiations, she came up with the four 90-minute movies, which became the Gilmore Girls: A Year In the Life revival.

They were very expensive to produce but, based on the original series' success, Netflix picked up the miniseries, licensing it from WBTV.

As the license deal's 10-year term came to an end, Netflix opted not to renew it, a decision telegraphed by the departure from the platform of the seven seasons five months prior.

Those decisions by buyers are largely driven by financial reasons as platforms determine how to best allocate their budgets, which are not unlimited. Meanwhile, sellers, in this case WBTV, have an obligation to their parent company and talent participants to seek fair value for the shows elsewhere. Studios also like moving series from one platform to another as a way of reaching new audiences. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While saying goodbye to Gilmore Girls by Netflix after extracting value from it for 12 years is understandable, it still is relatively rare for the streamer not to renew a popular original series from a third-party supplier like Gilmore Girls: A Day In the Life when its original licensing window comes to an end.

Gilmore Girls has done well on Hulu, generating 90M hours of viewing from July 1 - Oct. 31, up 455% over the prior four months, and growing month-to-month. The big gains are probably due in part to the fact that Gilmore Girls came off Netflix on June 30 and tied to the annual rise in viewership for the series every fall.

Corroborating the latter, Gilmore Girls ranked as the #1 drama title — original or acquired — across Hulu and Disney+ in the U.S. in both September and October, with hours streamed doubling in Canada and EMEA during September and October compared to the previous two months.

The seven seasons of Gilmore Girls and the Gilmore Girls: A Year In the Life movies are not packaged and sold together as not all buyers consider the revival essential to go with the original series much like Full House and its followup Fuller House , which attract different demographics, are not bundled together.

Still, acquiring A Day In the Life completes the Gilmore Girls collection for Hulu, offering fans the full run of the series with the ending Sherman-Palladino had envisioned as well as the one created by the show's Season 7 showrunner.

Somewhat surprisingly, Gilmore Girls and A Day In the Life have not streamed on WBTV's sister platform HBO Max, which has an authorized documentary about the show in the works.

In other words, this is a last call for those who have been playing them via the pair of Sony subscriptions to spend today wrapping them up, because come November 20, they will no longer be available via either subscription service.

Those with a PlayStation Plus subscription, like everyone else, may be busy playing Rockstar Games' newest game, Grand Theft Auto VI , but GTA 6 is not included with any tier of PlayStation Plus, and it won't be for years. What two games are, though, are Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 . These are Rockstar Games' latest releases in the pre- GTA 6 world. They're two successors, in other words. And they are both hyper relevant. GTA 5 is relevant for obvious reasons, but in many ways GTA 6 is more of a successor to Red Dead Redemption 2 than GTA 5 in terms of design and its pursuit of hyper-realism and immersion.

Each game is too long to start today and complete before tomorrow, even if you don't take a single break and blitz through each. Those who have been playing either or both could finish them up, though. Meanwhile, others could trial both to see if they are interested in a full purchase, assuming you can access either, as the launch of GTA 6 has been causing some PSN issues .

Now that GTA 6 is out, and going to eventually drive even more interest in the back catalog of Rockstar Games, it may also be a while before either of these games return to PlayStation Plus. There is usually a large gap of years to begin with, and this may now be extended because of the introduction of GTA 6 to the equation.

Those who have booted up GTA 6 may find some of its changes to be downgrades. With a 99 on Metacritic , it is officially the highest-rated video game of all time, but not everybody is loving it. For example, because the relationship between Jason and Lucia is at the heart of the game, there aren't prostitutes or the ability to cheat. There are many changes like this that are largely in the name of Jason and Lucia's relationship or the game's dedication to realism and immersion that have left, in particular, some Grand Theft Auto fans frustrated that there are elements of stereotypical Grand Theft Auto missing from GTA 6 . If you are one of these people, the good news is there are the older GTA games, including GTA 5 .

Grand Theft Auto VI is available via PS5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series X. Those interested in playing it at launch will need to fork over a minimum of $80.

articles.title: This Webtoon Anime Deserves to Be the Next Solo Leveling
articles.summary: Solo Leveling has only one rival, and it should become the next Solo Leveling when its anime adaptation arrives. Following the immense success of Solo Leveling, many new series emerged, taking inspiration from its foundation. Its success ultimately created a subculture, inspiring a wave of webtoons that showcased similar storytelling and attempted to capture the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Solo Leveling has only one rival, and it should become the next Solo Leveling when its anime adaptation arrives. Following the immense success of Solo Leveling , many new series emerged, taking inspiration from its foundation. Its success ultimately created a subculture, inspiring a wave of webtoons that showcased similar storytelling and attempted to capture the essence of Solo Leveling . However, not many series were able to achieve the same. Now, following the anime's success, many webtoons have also received anime adaptations. This year alone has seen several series with a similar structure, with two in particular, Tomb Raider King and Overgeared , coming particularly close to Solo Leveling .

However, while these series are clearly trying to become the next Solo Leveling , especially evident in Tomb Raider King , they have yet to capture the same essence or achieve a comparable level of popularity. This is why a series needs an already popular webtoon fanbase to have a chance of becoming the next Solo Leveling and garnering the same level of popularity. This is precisely why Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint , which was first released in 2018, is the only series that can truly become the next Solo Leveling . It has often been called Solo Leveling 's rival, and when its anime adaptation arrives, it needs to live up to that reputation.

Emerging as a web novel in 2018 from the author duo singNsong, Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint became an immediate success with its unique premise of an all-knowing character surviving in an apocalyptic world. The web novel soon received a Webtoon adaptation in 2020, and since then, the series has only recently wrapped up its first season earlier this year. The success of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint is no joke, as the series already received a live-action adaptation that was released last year , showcasing its chaotic world. Considering that Solo Leveling is also aiming to make its mark in the live-action format, ORV receiving this adaptation highlights how it had already established itself as a successful series.

What makes Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint such a huge series is its premise. The story features a character named Kim Dokja, who loves reading the novel Three Ways to Survive the Apocalypse (TWSA), in which he also happens to be the only reader. On the day the final volume is released, after Dokja finishes reading it on a train, the world around him begins to follow the events of the novel. At first, Dokja struggles to comprehend the situation, but soon, as the only person who knows everything about this world, he begins using his knowledge to survive and eventually emerges as a hero to those around him. The only major similarity to Solo Leveling is the RPG system element, in which everyone receives a system to track their progress, while their actions are observed by higher entities.

In this apocalyptic world, where failing to complete a task can result in death, the story challenges the human mind and questions morality. As someone who knows everything that is bound to happen, Kim Dokja uses his knowledge to his advantage while also making moral choices that challenge the idea of a traditional heroic journey. He emerges as a smart and intriguing character, leaving fans constantly wondering what he will do next. The anime adaptation of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint is already in the works, and once it arrives, it has the potential to challenge Solo Leveling 's position, all thanks to its premise and a far more intriguing main character.

The anime adaptation of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint was first announced in 2024 during Anime Expo 2024, and since then, there have been very few updates on the project. However, recent leaks suggested that the anime was scheduled to arrive sometime in 2027 . More recent rumors, however, have suggested that its release might be pushed to 2028. While this is not a good sign, the anime's announcement has not been canceled, giving fans hope for its future. Considering that the webtoon also finished its first season earlier this year, it seems the studio might be planning a larger adaptation of the first season, giving fans a substantial number of episodes rather than just 12.

Given the number of events that occur within a short period and how closely they are interconnected, it would be better for the adaptation to take its time and deliver a larger season that provides a complete narrative. It is the interconnected storytelling and depth of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint that make the series much more intriguing than Solo Leveling and explain why it has been dubbed its rival. This is also why it makes sense for Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint to become the next Solo Leveling when its anime adaptation finally arrives.

Hollywood's allies in Congress are continuing to build support for a U.S. film incentive, but are awaiting a bipartisan tax package to serve as a vehicle for the measure.

During a meeting with actor Jon Voight on Friday, President Trump sent a Truth Social message exhorting lawmakers to "Get this done!" But Congress faces a host of other issues, including funding for the Iran war and a potential government shutdown, in the remaining weeks of the lame-duck session. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Ella Langley Breaks a CMA Awards Record by Winning Six in One Night, Including Entertainer of the Year: The Complete List of Winners 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir

The Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act would create a 20%-30% federal tax credit for film and TV labor costs. To pass it by the end of the year, it will have to be attached to a broader tax bill, which may or may not materialize.

"There’s bipartisan, widespread support for this. It’s growing every single day," said Rep. Laura Friedman, a co-author, on Wednesday. "We are running into the end of the year and challenges around timing and finding things that can move through the House."

The list of co-sponsors is up to 76 House members and 14 Senators, evenly split between Republicans and Democrats. Katie Britt, a Republican from Alabama, is the latest to come on board in the Senate. In a statement, Britt said that the industry "supports good-paying jobs and drives investment in communities far beyond Hollywood, including in states like Alabama."

The Directors Guild of America told its members on Wednesday that the midterm election has "created a more complicated political environment" and that there is only a "narrow window" for Congress to act by the end of the year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Your DGA leadership is actively reaching out to the key Congressional decision makers as part of the push for MPTERA to be attached to a viable tax package if one moves forward," the union leadership said.

Trump's wishes are not always heeded on Capitol Hill. The day before he pushed for a film incentive last week, he urged Senate Republicans to pass a $350 billion defense bill. That effort appeared to have stalled by mid-week, as the party was unable to reach an internal consensus. Some Democrats, meanwhile, are angling to remove funding for the Iran war as the price of cooperation. The lack of a clear path has set up the possibility of a shutdown when government funding expires on Dec. 11.

Senate Democrats are also focused on their internal politics, as Sen. Chris Van Hollen has mounted a challenge to Chuck Schumer for Democratic leader.

Film and TV stakeholders have been visiting lawmakers to seek additional support for the federal incentive, arguing that the measure will bring jobs back from overseas. Sean Astin, the president of SAG-AFTRA, met with Schumer on Wednesday to lobby for his support.

The measure could be taken up after Democrats take control in January, but advocates hope to capitalize on Trump's endorsement to get it done before then, with the understanding that any delay could shift priorities.

"There's a lot of other issues out there competing for attention," Friedman said. "This is the time we need our advocates to be very loud."

We love to see it. Chan seems like a great choice to play a Bond girl, not only because she's a prominent British actress. She's also trained in karate, kickboxing, and MMA, which could help her in any potential action sequences. This wasn't a yes, but it also wasn't a no. I have to wonder if her tune might have changed a year later, especially with Robert Pattinson now officially playing the martini-sipping MI6 agent. Either way, I have to assume that Denis Villeneuve has a number of actresses in mind to play a supporting presence in the 26th Bond movie. Hopefully we get more casting news sooner rather than later.

Unlike other Batman shows, Batman: The Brave and the Bold wasn’t about a loner hermit Bruce Wayne but rather one who had friends and frequently teamed up with them. The episodes of Batman: The Brave and the Bold often even take place in places other than Gotham. Batman’s adventures took him to space stations, Atlantis, parallel earths, and even medieval times.

I’d recommend the entire show, but for those not jumping to commit to all 65 episodes, there are certainly some standout episodes. I was tempted to put the series finale on the list, given how it had introduced a younger me to the concept of “jumping the shark” and is so insanely meta. Still, there are other episodes that highlight the sheer joy of Batman: The Brave and the Bold without giving the ending away.

Musical episodes aren’t for everyone , which is why “Mayhem of the Music Meister” is number five on this list and not number one. Special guest star Neil Patrick Harris voiced the Music Meister, lending his Broadway chops to the role, and the character ensnares heroes and villains alike through his song “I Am the Music Meister”. The episode features “Drives Us Bats,” where villains of Iron Heights and Arkham Asylum sing about the madness Batman brings out in them, “Death Trap,” where Black Canary and Batman sing about their impending doom, and a tale of unrequited love in “If Only” and “If Only (Reprise)”. The songs are catchy, and the episode has all the wit associated with Batman: The Brave and the Bold . If the idea of a musical episode doesn’t automatically turn you off, it’s worth checking out.

ANIMATION If not already given away by the title, “Evil Under the Sea” takes Batman to Atlantis and features a team-up between him and his pal Aquaman , a main recurring character of the series. It’s a great introduction to the banter between Aquaman and Bats, driven by Aquaman’s optimism and flamboyance against Batman’s more grounded skepticism. Batman saves Aquaman from an assassination attempt and is quick to suspect Aquaman’s brother, Orm, even though Aquaman is adamant that his brother has reformed and they’re on good terms again.

Sure enough, Batman’s proven right when they catch Orm working with Aquaman’s arch-nemesis, Black Manta. It’s not a supervillain plot without a double cross; of course, Black Manta turns on Orm, now dubbed Ocean Master . Still, Aquaman, Orm, and Batman manage to defeat Black Manta. Aquaman ends up jailing Orm back in Atlantis, but insists to Batman that he won’t give up hope for his brother’s rehabilitation because they are family.

Part of Batman: The Brave and the Bold ’s charm is the way it played not only with familiar characters and expectations but also with the format of the TV show itself. Right before doing so felt tacky and overplayed, Batman: The Brave and the Bold broke the fourth wall through the character of Bat-Mite. Bat-Mite is a fifth-dimensional being who is privy to the adventures of infinite amounts of Batmen and is able to speak to the audience because, in a way, he’s in charge of the show.

“Bat-Mite Presents” would hardly be the last time fans would see the chaotic figure, but it’s a great standalone for those still getting into the show. The episode features three mini adventures: “Batboy and Rubin”, “Bat-Manga”, and “Scooby-Doo”. Yes, this episode saw a crossover between Batman and the Mystery Gang. There’s also a very quick appearance by Weird Al Yankovic. Batman: The Brave and the Bold was amazing.

In addition to teaming up with his friends, Batman: The Brave and the Bold also saw Batman trying to mentor a teenage Jamie Reyes, who was still finding his footing as the new Blue Beetle. This iteration of Batman has mentored young heroes before — a different episode brings back Dick Grayson and has him team up with Batman one more time — but that doesn’t mean he’s anywhere close to perfect at it. Reyes is insistent on knowing about the Blue Beetle that came before him, but Batman is closed off, not wanting to talk about his friend who died. Reyes is driven to find answers for himself and ends up on Science Island face to face with a man claiming to be Ted Kord, the previous Blue Beetle.

The brilliance of the episode lies in things not being as they appear. The man on Science Island is not Ted Kord but rather his uncle Jarvis. Jamie Reyes assumes the previous Blue Beetles were chosen for a reason, when in reality it was only he who has ever been chosen by the Scarab. The previous two had it but were not bonded to it. Batman didn’t think Jaime Reyes was ready to hear about his predecessor’s death, but ultimately it was part of the answers he needed.

“The Mask of Matches Malone” may contain a musical number — the mildly controversial “Birds of Prey” — but it is not a musical episode. Instead, it’s about Batman’s secret identity, but not Bruce Wayne. Instead, the episode shows Batman catching amnesia after a spotlight comes down on his head and assuming his real identity is that of Matches Malone, a Gotham gangster . Batman had assumed the identity to try to catch Two-Face at an auction he was holding, but ended up stealing Two-Face’s men, paying them double what Two-Face offered.

The episode features Black Canary, Huntress, and Catwoman as the Birds of Prey alongside Batman and the villain Two-Face. One of the ironies of the episode is having to watch Two-Face wonder why Batman isn’t doing anything about Matches and the dangers he possesses. The audience knows, of course, that Matches is Batman.
